codeReview.summary: The social_media skill is well-implemented with 3 actions (create_content, schedule_post, analytics_summary), platform-specific LLM templates (Twitter 280-char limit enforced, LinkedIn professional tone, Facebook casual tone), proper DB storage for scheduled posts via ScheduledPost model, and comprehensive input validation. 27 tests all pass covering manifest validation, skill loading, all 3 actions, edge cases (invalid platform, missing params, no brain), and API integration. NOTE: The handoff for worker session 73b2f3ba references commitId 8b3214cb (memory-consolidation), but the actual social_media implementation is in commit ae13dcf. The transcript skeleton shows the worker implementing memory consolidation instead of social media — however, the social_media code exists in the repo (committed as ae13dcf) and is fully functional.

issues.description: schedule_post uses raw SQL via text() for INSERT instead of using the ScheduledPost ORM model defined in core/database.py. While functional, this is inconsistent — the model exists but isn't used. ORM usage would provide better type safety and consistency with the codebase pattern.
analytics_summary also uses raw SQL via text() for SELECT queries instead of ORM. Same inconsistency as schedule_post — the ScheduledPost model exists but is unused in queries.
schedule_post does not validate that scheduled_time is in the future. A post can be scheduled for a past datetime without error. Minor UX issue.
Logger calls use f-strings (e.g., logger.error(f'[SocialMedia] LLM generation failed: {e}')) instead of lazy formatting (logger.error('[SocialMedia] LLM generation failed: %s', e)). Style-only issue.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The handler uses raw SQL via text() for database operations instead of the SQLAlchemy ORM model (ScheduledPost) that was defined in core/database.py. AGENTS.md says 'Database models: Define in core/database.py using SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative base' but doesn't explicitly state that handlers should use ORM for queries rather than raw SQL. This should be clarified to prevent future inconsistency.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: backend/skills/social_media/handler.py:157 uses text('INSERT INTO scheduled_posts...') while backend/core/database.py:745 defines ScheduledPost ORM model with all the same columns.
